# About this vignette

MAGeCK (Li et al. 2014, 2015) is the most used tool to find hits in pooled
screens. This vignette compares the hit-finding methods of ScreenR with MAGeCK
RRA and MAGeCK MLE on

1. simulated screens, where the true hits are known exactly;
2. a published K562 shRNA essentiality screen (`k562_count_table`), where
   the core essential genes are the true hits and the non-essential genes the
   true negatives;
3. the ScreenR example dataset (`count_table`), which has no ground truth.

MAGeCK is a Python program and cannot run while this vignette is built, so its
results (MAGeCK 0.5.9.5) and the simulation results are precomputed and
distributed in `inst/extdata/benchmark`. The ScreenR methods on the K562
screen are run here, so this vignette also shows how to compare ScreenR with
MAGeCK on your own data. The scripts that produced the precomputed results
are in the `benchmark` folder of the
[GitHub repository](https://github.com/EmanuelSoda/ScreenR).

```{r packages, message=FALSE}
library(ScreenR)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
benchmark_dir <- system.file("extdata", "benchmark", package = "ScreenR")
```

```{r labels}
labels <- c(
    MAGeCK_RRA = "MAGeCK RRA",
    MAGeCK_RRA_controls = "MAGeCK RRA (controls)",
    MAGeCK_MLE = "MAGeCK MLE",
    ScreenR_CAMERA = "CAMERA",
    ScreenR_CAMERA_storey = "CAMERA (Storey)",
    ScreenR_ROAST = "ROAST",
    ScreenR_FRY = "FRY",
    ScreenR_Zscore_mean = "Z-score (mean)",
    ScreenR_Zscore_median = "Z-score (median)",
    ScreenR_Zscore_controls = "Z-score (controls)",
    ScreenR_Zscore_edgeR = "Z-score (edgeR)",
    ScreenR_legacy_rule = "Legacy rule"
)
colours <- c(
    "MAGeCK RRA" = "#B2182B", "MAGeCK RRA (controls)" = "#EF8A62",
    "MAGeCK MLE" = "#67001F", "CAMERA" = "#2166AC",
    "CAMERA (Storey)" = "#67A9CF", "ROAST" = "#1B7837", "FRY" = "#7FBF7B",
    "Z-score (mean)" = "#762A83", "Z-score (median)" = "#C2A5CF",
    "Z-score (controls)" = "#DE77AE", "Z-score (edgeR)" = "#8C510A",
    "Legacy rule" = "grey50"
)
scenarios <- c(
    S0_null = "No hits", S1_baseline = "Baseline",
    S2_weak_effect = "Weak effect", S3_two_replicates = "2 replicates",
    S4_noisy = "Noisy", S5_off_target = "Off-target"
)
```

# Simulated screens

## Design

Each simulated screen has 500 genes with 10 shRNAs each and 500 non-targeting
shRNAs, with 3 control and 3 treated samples. The counts are negative
binomial, and the abundance of the shRNAs in the library is log-normal. 10% of
the genes are true hits, depleted in the treated samples: each of their shRNAs
has its own knockdown efficiency and 20% of them do not work at all. Six
scenarios were simulated, each with 5 random seeds:

| Scenario | Change from the baseline |
|---|---|
| No hits | no true hits: every call is false |
| Baseline | 3 vs 3 replicates, log2 fold change -1, dispersion 0.05 |
| Weak effect | log2 fold change -0.5 |
| 2 replicates | 2 vs 2 replicates |
| Noisy | dispersion 0.2 (four times more biological variability) |
| Off-target | 3% of the shRNAs depleted whatever gene they target |

The methods compared are MAGeCK RRA, MAGeCK RRA with the non-targeting
shRNAs as controls (`--control-sgrna`), MAGeCK MLE and the ScreenR methods:
`find_camera_hit()` (with Benjamini-Hochberg or Storey FDR),
`find_roast_hit()` (ROAST and FRY), `find_gene_zscore_hit()` (mean, median,
with the non-targeting shRNAs as reference and on the statistics of
`compute_barcode_statistics()`) and the legacy rule of `find_zscore_hit()`.

```{r load-simulation}
simulation <- read.csv(file.path(benchmark_dir, "simulation.csv")) %>%
    mutate(
        Method = factor(labels[method], levels = labels),
        Scenario = factor(scenarios[scenario], levels = scenarios)
    )
head(simulation)
```

For each method, screen and nominal FDR level (`alpha`) the table has the
number of genes called (`n_called`), the false discovery proportion (`FDP`,
the fraction of called genes that are not true hits), the true positive rate
(`TPR`), the fraction of genes without effect with p-value below `alpha`
(`null_p_below`), the area under the precision-recall curve of the p-value
ranking (`AUPRC`) and the run time in seconds.

## Are the p-values valid?

In the screens without hits, a valid test has about 5% of the genes with
p < 0.05.

```{r null-calibration, fig.height = 4}
simulation %>%
    filter(scenario == "S0_null", alpha == 0.05, method != "ScreenR_legacy_rule") %>%
    group_by(Method) %>%
    summarise(fraction = mean(null_p_below), se = sd(null_p_below) / sqrt(n())) %>%
    ggplot(aes(fraction, Method, colour = Method)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = fraction - 2 * se, xmax = fraction + 2 * se)) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours, guide = "none") +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
    labs(x = "Fraction of genes with p < 0.05 (no true hits)", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw()
```

All the methods are close to 5%. The legacy rule, which has no p-value,
called on average
`r round(mean(filter(simulation, scenario == "S0_null", method == "ScreenR_legacy_rule", alpha == 0.05)$n_called))`
genes in these screens, all of them false.

## Is the FDR controlled?

A method controls the FDR when the observed FDR (the mean false discovery
proportion) is at or below the nominal level, the dashed line.

```{r fdr-control, fig.height = 5}
simulation %>%
    filter(scenario != "S0_null", method != "ScreenR_legacy_rule") %>%
    group_by(Method, Scenario, alpha) %>%
    summarise(FDR = mean(FDP), .groups = "drop") %>%
    ggplot(aes(alpha, FDR, colour = Method)) +
    geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point(size = 1) +
    facet_wrap(~Scenario, nrow = 1) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2)) +
    labs(x = "Nominal FDR", y = "Observed FDR", colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90))
```

```{r fdr-table}
fdr_table <- simulation %>%
    filter(scenario != "S0_null", alpha == 0.05) %>%
    group_by(Method, Scenario) %>%
    summarise(FDP = mean(FDP), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Scenario, values_from = FDP)
knitr::kable(fdr_table, digits = 3,
    caption = "Observed FDR at a nominal FDR of 5% (mean over 5 seeds).")
```

CAMERA and the Z-score tests stay well below the nominal FDR in every
scenario. MAGeCK MLE exceeds it with off-target effects, MAGeCK RRA with the
non-targeting controls in every scenario, and the legacy rule has about 50%
false hits.

## How many hits are found?

```{r power, fig.height = 5}
simulation %>%
    filter(scenario != "S0_null", alpha == 0.05) %>%
    group_by(Method, Scenario) %>%
    summarise(TPR = mean(TPR), se = sd(TPR) / sqrt(n()), .groups = "drop") %>%
    ggplot(aes(Scenario, TPR, fill = Method)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colours) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "True positive rate at 5% FDR", fill = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The true positive rate depends on the FDR threshold, so it should be read
together with the previous section: the legacy rule finds almost all the hits
because it calls many false ones. The area under the precision-recall curve
measures how well the true hits are ranked first, whatever the threshold:

```{r auprc, fig.height = 5}
simulation %>%
    filter(scenario != "S0_null", alpha == 0.05, !is.na(AUPRC)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(Scenario, AUPRC, colour = Method)) +
    geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(0.85), width = 0.75,
        outlier.size = 0.5) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Area under the precision-recall curve",
        colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r summary-table}
simulation %>%
    filter(scenario != "S0_null", alpha == 0.05) %>%
    group_by(Method) %>%
    summarise(`Observed FDR` = mean(FDP), TPR = mean(TPR),
        AUPRC = mean(AUPRC), `Time (s)` = median(time)) %>%
    knitr::kable(digits = 3,
        caption = "Mean over the five scenarios with hits, at 5% FDR.")
```

CAMERA and the Z-score tests rank the hits as well as or better than MAGeCK
MLE in most scenarios and are about 200 times faster. At the same nominal
FDR they are more conservative: MAGeCK MLE finds more hits when the effects
are weak or the data noisy, but it does not control the FDR with off-target
effects. ROAST and FRY test each gene on its own barcodes, so they have
little power with two replicates or noisy data.

## Before and after the calibration of ScreenR 1.15.10

The first version of this benchmark showed that the ScreenR tests were valid
but too conservative (two-sided p-values used for a one-sided question and a
binomial gene test with few possible p-values). ScreenR 1.15.10 fixed both.

```{r before-after, fig.height = 3.5}
before <- read.csv(file.path(benchmark_dir, "simulation_before_1.15.10.csv"))
compared <- c("ScreenR_CAMERA", "ScreenR_ROAST", "ScreenR_Zscore_mean",
    "ScreenR_Zscore_edgeR")
bind_rows(
    before %>%
        mutate(method = recode(method, ScreenR_Zscore = "ScreenR_Zscore_mean"),
            version = "1.15.9"),
    simulation %>% mutate(version = "1.15.10")
) %>%
    filter(method %in% compared, scenario != "S0_null", alpha == 0.05) %>%
    mutate(Method = factor(labels[method], levels = labels),
        version = factor(version, c("1.15.9", "1.15.10"))) %>%
    group_by(Method, version) %>%
    summarise(TPR = mean(TPR), .groups = "drop") %>%
    ggplot(aes(TPR, Method, fill = version)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.75) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey70", "#2166AC")) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
    labs(x = "True positive rate at 5% FDR", y = NULL, fill = "ScreenR") +
    theme_bw()
```

# K562 essentiality screen

## The data

`k562_count_table` is a subset of the genome-wide shRNA screen of Morgens et
al. (2016): the plasmid library and two replicates after 14 days of growth of
K562 cells. The shRNAs of the genes needed for growth are depleted. The
reference genes of Hart et al. (`k562_reference_genes`) give the truth: the
681 core essential genes should be called, the 904 non-essential genes
should not.

```{r k562-object, message=FALSE}
data(k562_count_table)
data(k562_annotation_table)
data(k562_reference_genes)
samples <- data.frame(
    Sample = c("Plasmid", "T14_A", "T14_B"),
    Day = "Screen",
    Treatment = c("Plasmid", "T14", "T14")
)
k562 <- create_screenr_object(
    table = k562_count_table, annotation = k562_annotation_table,
    groups = factor(c("Plasmid", "T14", "T14")), sample_table = samples
)
k562 <- compute_data_table(normalize_data(k562))
k562
```

## Running the ScreenR methods

The comparison is day 14 against the plasmid. `fdr = 1` returns every gene, so
that the methods can be evaluated at any threshold.

```{r k562-screenr}
design <- create_design_matrix(k562)
contrast <- create_contrast(design, treatment = "T14", control = "Plasmid")
metrics <- compute_metrics(k562,
    control = "Plasmid", treatment = "T14", day = "Screen"
)
results <- list(
    `ScreenR_CAMERA` = find_camera_hit(k562, design, contrast,
        fdr = 1, number_barcode = 1),
    `ScreenR_FRY` = find_roast_hit(k562, design, contrast,
        method = "fry", fdr = 1, number_barcode = 1),
    `ScreenR_Zscore_mean` = find_gene_zscore_hit(metrics,
        fdr = 1, min_barcodes = 1, n_permutations = 20000, seed = 1),
    `ScreenR_Zscore_controls` = find_gene_zscore_hit(metrics,
        control_genes = "non-targeting", fdr = 1, min_barcodes = 1,
        n_permutations = 20000, seed = 1)
)
results <- lapply(results, function(x) select(x, Gene, PValue, FDR))
```

## Adding the MAGeCK results

MAGeCK was run on the same counts (`mageck test` for RRA and `mageck mle`
with a design with intercept and treatment); for MAGeCK MLE the depletion
p-value is computed from the Wald statistic.

```{r k562-mageck}
mageck <- read.csv(file.path(benchmark_dir, "mageck_k562.csv"))
results <- c(split(select(mageck, -method), mageck$method), results)
names(results)
```

## Evaluation on the reference genes

```{r k562-evaluate}
evaluate <- function(result, alpha = 0.05) {
    # Genes are sorted by name, so that tied p-values are ordered the same
    # way for every method
    merged <- left_join(k562_reference_genes, result, by = "Gene") %>%
        mutate(PValue = coalesce(PValue, 1), FDR = coalesce(FDR, 1)) %>%
        arrange(Gene)
    essential <- merged$Class == "core essential"
    called <- merged$FDR <= alpha
    hit <- essential[order(merged$PValue)]
    precision <- cumsum(hit) / seq_along(hit)
    tibble(
        `Essential called` = sum(called & essential),
        `Non-essential called` = sum(called & !essential),
        Recall = mean(called[essential]),
        `Non-essential fraction` = sum(called & !essential) / max(1, sum(called)),
        AUPRC = sum(precision[hit]) / sum(hit)
    )
}
k562_evaluation <- bind_rows(lapply(results, evaluate), .id = "method") %>%
    mutate(Method = labels[method]) %>%
    select(Method, everything(), -method)
knitr::kable(k562_evaluation, digits = 3,
    caption = "K562: reference genes called at 5% FDR.")
```

```{r k562-pr, fig.height = 5, fig.width = 6.5}
precision_recall <- bind_rows(lapply(results, function(result) {
    merged <- left_join(k562_reference_genes, result, by = "Gene") %>%
        mutate(PValue = coalesce(PValue, 1)) %>%
        arrange(Gene)
    hit <- merged$Class[order(merged$PValue)] == "core essential"
    tibble(recall = cumsum(hit) / sum(hit),
        precision = cumsum(hit) / seq_along(hit))
}), .id = "method") %>%
    mutate(Method = factor(labels[method], levels = labels))
ggplot(precision_recall, aes(recall, precision, colour = Method)) +
    geom_line() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = colours) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.4, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Recall (core essential genes)", y = "Precision", colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw()
```

The Z-score test (mean) and CAMERA call about as many essential genes as
MAGeCK RRA with few non-essential genes, and the Z-score test ranks the genes
as well as MAGeCK RRA and better than MAGeCK MLE. MAGeCK MLE finds more
essential genes but also many non-essential ones (MAGeCK MLE skipped the
genes with more than about 40 shRNAs, which count as not called here).

Two ScreenR results show the limits of some methods:

* **FRY calls no gene.** It tests each gene on its own barcodes and relies on
  the variability between replicates, but the control group is a single
  plasmid sample. With one control sample use CAMERA or the Z-score test.
* **The non-targeting reference calls hundreds of non-essential genes.** In
  shRNA screens the targeting shRNAs are usually somewhat depleted compared
  with the non-targeting ones, so every gene looks depleted against them.
  Before using `control_genes`, check that the controls behave like genes
  without effect:

```{r k562-controls, fig.height = 3.5}
metrics %>%
    left_join(distinct(k562_annotation_table, Gene, Class), by = "Gene") %>%
    filter(Class %in% c("non-targeting", "non-essential", "core essential")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(Log2FC, colour = Class)) +
    geom_density() +
    labs(x = "Barcode log2 fold change (day 14 vs plasmid)", colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw()
```

The non-targeting shRNAs (the reference) are shifted to the right of the
non-essential genes, so they are not a good model of a gene without effect.

# ScreenR example dataset

The example dataset has no ground truth, so we only measure the agreement
between the methods on the day 4 comparison of treated and control samples.

```{r example-data, message=FALSE}
data(count_table)
data(annotation_table)
counts <- count_table
colnames(counts) <- c(
    "Barcode", "Time1", "Time2", "Time3_TRT_A", "Time3_TRT_B", "Time3_TRT_C",
    "Time3_CTRL_A", "Time3_CTRL_B", "Time3_CTRL_C",
    "Time4_TRT_A", "Time4_TRT_B", "Time4_TRT_C",
    "Time4_CTRL_A", "Time4_CTRL_B", "Time4_CTRL_C"
)
counts <- filter(counts, Barcode != "*")
groups <- factor(c(
    "T1/T2", "T1/T2",
    rep("Time3_TRT", 3), rep("Time3_CTRL", 3),
    rep("Time4_TRT", 3), rep("Time4_CTRL", 3)
))
object <- create_screenr_object(
    table = counts, annotation = annotation_table, groups = groups
)
object <- compute_data_table(normalize_data(remove_all_zero_row(object)))
design <- create_design_matrix(object)
contrast <- create_contrast(design, "Time4_TRT", "Time4_CTRL")
metrics <- compute_metrics(object,
    control = "CTRL", treatment = "TRT", day = "Time4"
)
example <- list(
    ScreenR_CAMERA = find_camera_hit(object, design, contrast,
        fdr = 1, number_barcode = 1),
    ScreenR_FRY = find_roast_hit(object, design, contrast,
        method = "fry", fdr = 1, number_barcode = 1),
    ScreenR_Zscore_mean = find_gene_zscore_hit(metrics,
        fdr = 1, min_barcodes = 1, n_permutations = 20000, seed = 1)
)
example <- lapply(example, function(x) select(x, Gene, PValue, FDR))
mageck <- read.csv(file.path(benchmark_dir, "mageck_screenr_dataset.csv"))
example <- c(split(select(mageck, -method), mageck$method), example)
```

```{r example-correlation, fig.height = 4, fig.width = 5.5}
genes <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(example, function(x) as.character(x$Gene)))
ranks <- sapply(example, function(x) {
    rank(x$PValue[match(genes, as.character(x$Gene))])
})
colnames(ranks) <- labels[colnames(ranks)]
as.data.frame(as.table(cor(ranks, method = "spearman"))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(Var1, Var2, fill = Freq)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Freq)), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "#2166AC", limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Spearman") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r example-hits}
vapply(example, function(x) sum(x$FDR <= 0.05), integer(1))
```

The treatment effect in the example dataset is weak and few genes pass 5%
FDR. The rankings of the ScreenR methods agree well with MAGeCK MLE and less
with MAGeCK RRA.

# Recommendations

* Use `find_gene_zscore_hit()` or `find_camera_hit()` to call hits: they
  control the FDR, rank the hits as well as MAGeCK and run in seconds. Use
  `statistic = "median"` when off-target effects are a concern.
* Use `find_roast_hit()` (ROAST or FRY) only with replicates in both groups.
* Keep the default reference of `find_gene_zscore_hit()` unless the control
  genes are shown to behave like genes without effect.
* Do not use the legacy rule of `find_zscore_hit()` to call hits: about half
  of its hits are false.

# Literature

* Li W, Xu H, Xiao T et al. (2014). MAGeCK enables robust identification of
  essential genes from genome-scale CRISPR/Cas9 knockout screens. Genome Biol
  15:554.
* Li W, Köster J, Xu H et al. (2015). Quality control, modeling, and
  visualization of CRISPR screens with MAGeCK-VISPR. Genome Biol 16:281.
* Morgens DW, Deans RM, Li A, Bassik MC (2016). Systematic comparison of
  CRISPR/Cas9 and RNAi screens for essential genes. Nat Biotechnol
  34:634-636.
* Hart T, Brown KR, Sircoulomb F, Rottapel R, Moffat J (2014). Measuring
  error rates in genomic perturbation screens: gold standards for human
  functional genomics. Mol Syst Biol 10:733.
